title: Sandworm_Backdoor_Investigation_750
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sandworm intrusion set, specifically targeting Centreon systems with the Exaramel backdoor. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat posed by this backdoor, which provides remote access and control capabilities to the attackers.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes.
Determine persistence mechanisms used by the backdoor.
Analyze network traffic for command-and-control (C2) communication.
Collect forensic evidence and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sandworm intrusion set, specifically targeting Centreon systems with the Exaramel backdoor. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat posed by this backdoor, which provides remote access and control capabilities to the attackers.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the username 'cyrano' and password 'cyrano' and enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the username 'cyrano' and password 'cyrano' and enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target system, you notice unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services that might be responsible for this activity.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service in this case is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is not a standard system service and is likely related to the unusual network activity.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the backdoor.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can use the `systemctl list-timers` command to list all systemd timers. Look for any timers that are associated with the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism in this case is a systemd timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to find how the service is scheduled to run.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-timers` command to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The persistence mechanism involves a systemd timer that triggers the suspicious service.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication to better understand the threat.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for C2 communication, you can use the `ss -tulnp` command to list all listening ports. Look for any ports that are associated with the suspicious service. The network port used for C2 communication in this case is 4444.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Analyze network connections and listen ports to identify the port used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ss -tulnp` command to list all listening ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is listening on a non-standard port, which is likely used for C2 communication.
